name: Archaeological Site of Volubilis
description: Volubilis is a ruined Roman city set among wheat and olive fields near Meknes, Morocco, on the empire's far southwestern edge. Founded in the 3rd century BC, it grew rich on olive oil, and you can still walk past a triumphal arch, a basilica and grand town houses with colourful mosaic floors. It later briefly served as the seat of Idris I, founder of Morocco's first Islamic dynasty.
